name: Pantheism
plain_explanation: The view that God and the world are not really separate -- that everything that exists is, in some sense, part of God.
precise_definition: The doctrine that God and the world are not distinct, so that everything in the world is part of God; developed most fully, in Russell's later account, by Spinoza, but attractive to mystics generally.
why_it_mattered: Russell uses it as the foil against which Augustine's insistence on creation ex nihilo, and his freedom from mystical difficulty about the world's separateness from God, stands out.
historical_origin: Recurs, per Russell, as a natural consequence of the Greek view that creation from nothing is impossible.
competing_positions: Augustine's orthodox insistence, following Genesis, that the world is created and stands outside God
connection_to_politics_or_religion: A recurring temptation for Christian mystics, who have historically found orthodoxy on this point difficult to maintain.
